conditions: An operation requires atomic visibility of multiple database writes
lesson: Place the required writes within the same atomic boundary and test rollback at intermediate failure points.
tradeoffs: Transaction scope affects contention and availability.
provenance: Original short engineering inference based on the linked PostgreSQL transaction documentation; source text is not redistributed.

problem: An atomic transaction alone does not specify concurrent invariant protection
conditions: Concurrent transactions read and update related records
lesson: Specify the required isolation or locking mechanism and its retry handling; inspect concurrent schedules that might violate the business invariant.
tradeoffs: Stronger isolation can require transaction retries.
provenance: Original short engineering inference based on the linked PostgreSQL isolation documentation; source text is not redistributed.

problem: A replica can lag an acknowledged write
conditions: Reads are routed to a standby
The application requires a read guarantee stronger than eventual consistency
lesson: Describe the synchronization and read-routing boundary explicitly. Replication being configured does not by itself establish read-your-writes or linearizability.
tradeoffs: Waiting for replay or choosing a different read route changes latency and availability.
provenance: Original short engineering inference based on PostgreSQL standby documentation; source text is not redistributed.

problem: Serving stale responses during an error can extend cache age
conditions: Cached responses have a maximum permitted age
Failure behavior can serve an older response
lesson: Include error paths and invalidation delays in the freshness bound. A normal-path TTL alone does not describe all permitted stale responses.
tradeoffs: Rejecting stale reads can reduce availability during source failure.
provenance: Original short engineering inference based on HTTP caching semantics; HTTP-specific rules do not automatically apply to every application cache.

conditions: A lock or writer can outlive a promotion or lease boundary
lesson: Test whether the old owner can still mutate storage after promotion. Record how storage rejects obsolete ownership, rather than relying on the existence of a lock service.
tradeoffs: Enforced fencing adds coordination and storage-side validation.
provenance: Original engineering inference motivated by the documented asynchronous-replication lock race and lock validity limits; this is not a claim that Redis alone implements the proposed fencing.

problem: Retries amplify load or exceed a request deadline
conditions: A dependency call can be retried
A total request deadline and finite resources are required
lesson: Account for every attempt and delay in the deadline, bound retries across layers, and spread retries with jitter to avoid synchronized retry load.
tradeoffs: Fewer retries may reduce immediate recovery from transient failures.
provenance: Original short engineering inference based on AWS Builders Library; source text is not redistributed.
